prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "book", with the standing line "A nine-chapter guide to the server that turns an Ethereum address into an annotated PNG, with live progress." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A single request travels left to right. A client sends a request naming a series and an address. The request reaches a validation gate and then a cache check. From the cache check, one short branch goes straight to a finished image. The main branch passes a lock and enters a long horizontal track of eight phase stations: setup, base prompts, enhance prompt, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate, completed. Above the track, a return loop arcs back to the client, carrying a progress document. The loop repeats until the document reads done=true. The track ends at an annotated PNG leaving toward the lower right.

Magnified circles set beside it show First circle, the cache hit: an existing image short-circuits the whole track. Second circle, the lock: two identical requests arrive, only one generation runs, and the second request only watches progress. Third circle, skip mode: with no API key, the image station is replaced by a simulated step, and the track still runs to completion.

Colour is used so that Vermilion marks the path of one request and its polling loop. Teal marks anything already on disk, such as cached and finished images. Ochre marks protection, meaning the lock and the validation gate.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 8 phases along the track, counted with tick marks. 9 chapters in the row of spines. 3 request forms in the row of studies: plain, generate, remove. A 1-second polling interval marked on the return loop. A 5m lock lifetime marked as a dimension beside the lock.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: series and address sit on the incoming request. validate sits on the gate. cache check and cache hit sit on the short branch. lock sits at the track entrance. The phase names sit on their stations: setup, enhance prompt, image wait, annotate, completed. progress JSON and done=true sit on the return loop. ?generate=1 sits on the triggering request. plain GET and streams PNG sit on the first study. ?remove=1 and prompts persist sit on the third study. annotated PNG, prompt files, /preview and newest first sit in the outputs group. skip mode sits on the simulated image step.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: series, address, validate, cache check, lock, setup, enhance prompt, image wait, annotate, completed, progress JSON, ?generate=1, done=true cache hit, one generation, skip mode, no API key plain GET, streams PNG, ?remove=1, prompts persist annotated PNG, prompt files, /preview, newest first nine chapters, Getting Started, Progress & Polling, Configuration

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Duplicate requests only watch the same progress; Poll once per second until finished. Existing image skips all work; Without a key, image step is simulated. Removing deletes only the image. Final image served at the same address; Gallery groups images by series, newest first. Documents the server, not the library.
